Why This Book Exists


Imagine someone handed you a letter. The letter was written 1,000 years ago. It describes your life. It describes the town you were born in. It describes the way you would die. It describes the words people would say at your funeral. You would be stunned. You would want to know who wrote it. You would want to know how they knew.


The Bible makes a claim just like this. It contains over 300 predictions about a coming figure called the Messiah. These predictions are called prophecies. They are not vague guesses. They are specific details. They name the town He would be born in. They name the price a friend would sell Him for. They describe the way His hands and feet would be pierced. They describe the words people would mock Him with while He hung on a cross.


These prophecies were written by different authors. They lived in different centuries. They came from different backgrounds. Some were kings. Some were shepherds. Some were farmers. They wrote over a period of 1,500 years. And they all pointed to one person. That person is Jesus.


This book is for the curious. It is for the spiritual seeker who wants evidence. It is for the person who is not satisfied with blind faith. Over the next 30 days, we are going to look at 30 of these ancient predictions. We are going to see what they said. We are going to see how they were fulfilled. And we are going to see the code. The code is Jesus.


The Value You Will Get


By the end of this book, you will not see the Bible as a collection of old stories. You will see it as a supernatural blueprint. You will understand the math behind the prophecies. You will understand why they are so specific. You will understand why they are impossible to fake. And you will see the code. You will have a ...

pages.body:
The Hook
Imagine you are watching a movie. It is a mystery. The detective is looking for the bad guy. The bad guy is a snake. The snake is sneaky. The snake is dangerous. The snake has caused a lot of trouble. But then the detective finds a clue. The clue says a hero is coming. The hero will crush the snake's head. The hero will win. That clue is in the very first book of the Bible. It is the first prophecy. It is the first code.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"And I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your offspring and hers; he will crush your head, and you will strike his heel." - Genesis 3:15 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


This is the first prophecy in the Bible. God is speaking to a snake. But He is not just speaking to a snake. He is speaking to the devil. He is speaking to the enemy. He says a descendant of a woman will come. That descendant will crush the serpent's head. The serpent will strike his heel. It sounds like a riddle. It sounds like a code. It is the first clue in the greatest mystery of all time.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"But when the set time had fully come, God sent his Son, born of a woman, born under the law..." - Galatians 4:4


Jesus is that descendant. He was born of a woman. He came to crush the serpent's head. He came to defeat the devil. On the cross, it looked like the serpent won. The heel was struck. Jesus died. But three days later, He rose from the dead. The serpent's head was crushed. The code was cracked. The hero had won.


The Verdict
This is not a coincidence. The first prophecy in the Bible is about a hero. The greatest hero in the Bible is Jesus. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The code is Jesus.


The Resonance
Do you feel like the snake is winning? Do you feel like the enemy is too strong? Do you feel like you are losing the battle? Remember the first prophecy. The hero is coming. The hero has come. The serpent's head is crushed. You are on the winning side.


The Prayer
God, thank you for the first prophecy. Thank you for the promise of a hero. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you for crushing the serpent's head. Thank you for winning the victory. Help me to live in that victory today. Amen.

pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever made a promise? Have you ever made a promise you knew you could not keep? We do it all the time. We promise to pay someone back. We promise to be somewhere. We promise to change. We break promises. But God is different. God made a promise to a man. The man was old. The man had no children. The man was a nomad. But God promised him a family. God promised him a blessing. God promised him a descendant.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"I will bless those who bless you, and whoever curses you I will curse; and all peoples on earth will be blessed through you." - Genesis 12:3 (Written around 2000 B.C.)


God spoke to Abraham. He told him to leave his home. He told him to go to a new land. He gave him a promise. He said, "I will bless you. I will make your name great. You will be a blessing. All peoples on earth will be blessed through you." This was a huge promise. It meant that one day, someone from Abraham's family would change the world. Not just one nation. Not just one tribe. The whole world. Every skin color. Every language. Every person.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"This is the genealogy of Jesus the Messiah the son of David, the son of Abraham..." - Matthew 1:1


The Gospel of Matthew opens with a family tree. It traces the line of Jesus back to Abraham. It shows that Jesus is a descendant of Abraham. He is the one who brings blessing to the whole world. Through Jesus, people from every nation can be forgiven. Through Jesus, people from every language can be saved. The promise to the old nomad came true in the baby born in Bethlehem.


The Verdict
For this prophecy to be fulfilled, the Messiah had to be Jewish. He had to come from a specific family line. The odds of this being a coincidence are tiny. The Bible traces the lineage from Abraham to Jesus with precision. It is another brick in the wall of evidence.


The Resonance
You are not an accident. You are part of a bigger story. God's plan is not just for one person. It is not just for one group. It is for the whole world. And you are included. You are part of the blessing.


The Prayer
God, thank you for keeping your promises. Thank you that your plan has always been bigger than one person or one nation. Thank you that Jesus came to bless the whole world, including me. Help me to see that I am part of your story. Help me to share the blessing with others. Amen.

The Hook
Have you ever watched a royal wedding? The dresses. The crowns. The gold. It looks fancy. It looks regal. It looks like a storybook. But have you ever wondered where the royal family comes from? Have you ever wondered where the line of kings begins? In the Bible, there is a prediction about a royal line. It was spoken by a dying old man to his sons. And it is a code.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"The scepter will not depart from Judah, nor the ruler's staff from between his feet, until he to whom it belongs shall come and the obedience of the nations shall be his." - Genesis 49:10 (Written around 1800 B.C.)


Jacob was dying. He was old. He was blind. He called his twelve sons to his bed. He gave each son a blessing. He gave each son a prophecy. When he got to Judah, he said something strange. He said the scepter would not depart from Judah. A scepter is a stick a king holds. It is a sign of authority. Jacob was saying that the line of kings would come from Judah. He was saying that one day, the ultimate King would come. And He would rule the nations.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"For it is clear that our Lord descended from Judah..." - Hebrews 7:14


Jesus was from the tribe of Judah. The New Testament makes this clear. He is the King of Kings. He is the one who will rule the nations. The dying words of Jacob were not just a family blessing. They were a prophecy about Jesus. The code was cracked.


The Verdict
The Jewish people had twelve tribes. They were all different. They all had different roles. But the Messiah had to come from one specific tribe. The odds of this being random are small. The Bible got it right. It is another clue. It is another piece of evidence.


The Resonance
History is not random. It is not just a bunch of accidents. There is a pattern hidden in the chaos. God is not just watching. God is directing. The blueprint is real. The code is real.


The Prayer
God, you are the King of Kings. Thank you for your plan that unfolds across thousands of years. Thank you that you are in control of history. Thank you that you are in control of my history. Help me to trust you with my future. Help me to trust you with my life. Amen.
pages.title: Day 3: The Scepter of Judah

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever looked up at the night sky and felt small? The stars are beautiful. They are also mysterious. They have guided travelers for centuries. Sailors use them to navigate the oceans. Shepherds use them to track the seasons. But in the Bible, a star is used for something else. It is used as a sign. It is used as a code. It points to a king.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"I see him, but not now; I behold him, but not near. A star will come out of Jacob; a scepter will rise out of Israel." - Numbers 24:17 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


These words were spoken by a pagan prophet named Balaam. He was not an Israelite. He was not a follower of God. But God used him to speak a prophecy. Balaam looked at the people of Israel and he said, "I see him, but not now." He saw a future figure. He said a star would come out of Jacob. He said a scepter would rise out of Israel. He was predicting a king. He was predicting the Messiah.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"Where is the one who has been born king of the Jews? We saw his star when it rose and have come to worship him." - Matthew 2:2


When Jesus was born, wise men came from the east. They were star gazers. They saw a star in the sky. They knew the ancient prophecy. They knew a star would signal the birth of a king. They traveled hundreds of miles to find Him. The star led them to the house where Jesus was. They bowed down and worshiped Him.


The Verdict
This is a strange prophecy. It was spoken by a nonbeliever. It was spoken 1,400 years before Jesus was born. It connects a star to a king. And the story of the wise men lines up perfectly. It is another clue in the code.


The Resonance
The stars themselves were pointing to a king. The universe is not silent. It speaks. It points. If the stars can point to a king, maybe there is a God who wants to be found. Maybe there is a God who is calling you.


The Prayer
God, the heavens declare your glory. Thank you for putting signs in the sky that point to Jesus. Thank you for the wise men who followed the star. Help me to follow the clues that lead to you. Help me to seek you with all my heart. Amen.
pages.title: Day 4: The Star out of Jacob

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever had a mentor? Someone who taught you everything you know? Maybe a coach. Maybe a boss. Maybe a parent. Moses was the ultimate mentor for the people of Israel. He led them out of slavery. He gave them the law. He talked to God face to face. But Moses said there was someone else coming. Someone even greater than him. It is a code.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"I will raise up for them a prophet like you from among their fellow Israelites, and I will put my words in his mouth. He will tell them everything I command him." - Deuteronomy 18:18 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


Moses was talking to the people. He said, "God will raise up a prophet like me." This was a massive claim. Moses was the greatest prophet in Jewish history. He was the one who parted the Red Sea. He was the one who received the Ten Commandments. But he said someone else was coming. This new prophet would speak God's words. The people were supposed to listen to Him.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"For Moses said, 'The Lord your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your own people; you must listen to everything he tells you.'" - Acts 3:22


Peter quotes this prophecy in the book of Acts. He applies it to Jesus. Jesus is the new Moses. Moses led people out of physical slavery in Egypt. Jesus leads people out of spiritual slavery to sin. Moses gave the law. Jesus gives grace. Moses spoke to God face to face. Jesus is God.


The Verdict
The Jews were waiting for this prophet. They asked John the Baptist, "Are you the prophet?" They knew the prophecy. They were looking for someone like Moses. Jesus fulfilled that expectation. He was the greater Moses. The code was cracked.


The Resonance
We are not just looking for a teacher. We are looking for a liberator. A teacher can tell you what to do. A liberator can set you free. Jesus is both. He teaches us the truth. He sets us free from sin.


The Prayer
God, thank you for sending Jesus. He is greater than Moses. He speaks your words. Help me to listen to Him. Help me to follow Him. Set me free from the things that hold me back. Amen.
pages.title: Day 5: The Prophet Like Moses

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever seen a tree stump? It looks dead. It looks finished. It is just a flat piece of wood in the ground. It is easy to think nothing will ever grow there again. But sometimes a tiny green shoot pushes up through the dead wood. It is a sign of life. That is what Isaiah saw. He saw a dead stump. But he also saw a shoot. It is a code.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"A shoot will come up from the stump of Jesse; from his roots a Branch will bear fruit." - Isaiah 11:1 (Written around 700 B.C.)


Jesse was the father of King David. David was a great king. He was a man after God's own heart. But his family line looked like a dead stump. Israel was in trouble. The kingdom was divided. The kings were weak. It looked like the royal line was finished. But Isaiah said, "A shoot will come up from the stump of Jesse." He said a Branch would bear fruit. This was a promise that the royal line would not die. A new king was coming.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"And again, Isaiah says, 'The Root of Jesse will spring up, one who will arise to rule over the nations; in him the Gentiles will hope.'" - Romans 15:12


Jesus is that Branch. He came from the line of David. He came from the stump of Jesse. He is the King who rose from a dead family line. And Paul says something amazing in Romans. He says the Gentiles will hope in Him. This Branch is not just for one nation. He is for the whole world. The code was cracked.


The Verdict
The prophet Isaiah said a dead stump would come alive. He said the royal line would continue. Four hundred years passed. The line seemed dead. Then Jesus was born. The Branch grew. The prophecy was fulfilled.


The Resonance
God specializes in bringing life out of broken things. Are you feeling like a dead stump? Are you feeling like something in your life is finished? Maybe a dream died. Maybe a relationship ended. God can bring a green shoot. He can bring new life.


The Prayer
God, you bring life out of dead things. Thank you for the Branch that grew from the stump of Jesse. Thank you for Jesus. I ask you to bring new life to the broken places in my heart. Bring new life to my dreams. Bring new life to my family. Amen.
pages.title: Day 6: The Root of Jesse

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever heard someone say, "That is impossible?" Maybe you said it when you saw a magic trick. Maybe you said it when someone told you a story that seemed too good to be true. The Bible makes an impossible claim. It says the Messiah would be born of a virgin. This is a biological impossibility. It is a miracle. And it was predicted 700 years before it happened. It is a code.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign: The virgin will conceive and give birth to a son, and will call him Immanuel." - Isaiah 7:14 (Written around 700 B.C.)


Isaiah was speaking to a king named Ahaz. Ahaz was a wicked king. He was worried about enemies. God told him to ask for a sign. Ahaz refused. So God said, "I will give you a sign anyway." And the sign was a virgin giving birth. The child would be called Immanuel. Immanuel means "God with us." This was not a normal baby. This was God coming to earth.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"The virgin will conceive and give birth to a son, and they will call him Immanuel" (which means "God with us"). - Matthew 1:23


Matthew tells us that Jesus is the fulfillment of this prophecy. Mary was a virgin. She became pregnant by the power of the Holy Spirit. She gave birth to Jesus. He is God with us. The code was cracked.


The Verdict
This is a prophecy about a miracle. It cannot be explained away by coincidence. It cannot be explained by natural means. It requires a supernatural event. If the prophecy is true, then Jesus is not just a good teacher. He is God.


The Resonance
We serve a God who does impossible things. Are you facing an impossible situation? A problem no doctor can fix? A relationship no counselor can fix? A financial situation no bank can fix? God can do the impossible. He is the God of the impossible.


The Prayer
God, you are the God of the impossible. Thank you for sending Jesus, born of a virgin. Thank you that you are with us. Help me to believe that you can do impossible things in my life. Help me to trust you with the impossible. Amen.
pages.title: Day 7: Born of a Virgin

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Where were you born? Maybe you were born in a big city. Maybe you were born in a small town. Maybe you were born in a hospital. The place of your birth matters. It is part of your identity. The Bible predicted the exact location of the Messiah's birth. It was not a big city. It was a tiny town. It is a code.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, though you are small among the clans of Judah, out of you will come for me one who will be ruler over Israel, whose origins are from of old, from ancient times." - Micah 5:2 (Written around 700 B.C.)


Micah was a prophet. He was looking at the towns of Judah. He said, "Bethlehem, you are small." Bethlehem was a small town. It was not a capital. It was not a major city. But Micah said the ruler of Israel would come from Bethlehem. This was a specific address. It was a prophecy with a zip code. It was a code.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"So Joseph also went up from the town of Nazareth in Galilee to Judea, to Bethlehem the town of David, because he belonged to the house and line of David." - Luke 2:4


Joseph and Mary lived in Nazareth. They were far from Bethlehem. But the Roman emperor Caesar Augustus ordered a census. Every person had to go to their ancestral town to register. Joseph was from the line of David. David was from Bethlehem. So Joseph traveled to Bethlehem. And Mary went with him. She was pregnant. She gave birth in Bethlehem. The tiny town. The specific address. The code was cracked.


The Verdict
It is statistically impossible to orchestrate your own birthplace. You cannot control where you are born. But the prophet knew. He named the town. And the Roman census made it happen. The empire unknowingly played a part in God's plan.


The Resonance
God pays attention to details. If He cared enough to arrange the exact birthplace of His son, He cares about the details of your life. He cares about your address. He cares about your family. He cares about the small things.


The Prayer
God, thank you for caring about details. Thank you for planning every step of your son's life. Thank you that you care about my life too. Help me to trust you with the small things. Help me to trust you with the big things. Amen.
pages.title: Day 8: Born in Bethlehem

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever met a child who was wise beyond their years? Maybe they said something that surprised you. They seemed to understand things that other kids did not. Now imagine a baby who is not just wise. Imagine a baby who is God. That is what Isaiah predicted. He said the coming child would be called Mighty God. It is a code.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"For to us a child is born, to us a son is given, and the government will be on his shoulders. And he will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace." - Isaiah 9:6 (Written around 700 B.C.)


These are big titles. Wonderful Counselor. Mighty God. Everlasting Father. Prince of Peace. These are not titles for a normal child. These are titles for God. Isaiah said the child would be God. This was a radical claim. The Jews believed in one God. But Isaiah said the child would be God in the flesh. It was a code.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"I and the Father are one." - John 10:30


Jesus made a claim that shocked everyone. He said, "I and the Father are one." He was saying He is God. He was saying He is the Mighty God. The religious leaders tried to kill Him for saying this. They knew what He meant. They knew He was claiming to be God. The code was cracked.


The Verdict
Jesus did not just claim to be a prophet. He did not just claim to be a teacher. He claimed to be God. The prophecy said the child would be Mighty God. Jesus claimed to be Mighty God. This is another piece of evidence. This is another clue in the code.


The Resonance
Spirituality is not just about reaching up. The Divine reached down. God did not just send a message. He sent Himself. He came in the form of a baby. He came to be with us.


The Prayer
Jesus, you are Mighty God. Thank you for coming to earth. Thank you for stepping down from heaven. Thank you for being the Everlasting Father. Help me to know you more. Help me to love you more. Amen.
pages.title: Day 9: The Everlasting Father

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever had to run away from something? Maybe you ran away from a bully. Maybe you ran away from a mistake. Maybe you ran away from a situation you could not handle. The Bible tells us that Jesus had to run away. He had to be a refugee. He had to flee to Egypt. It is a code.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"When Israel was a child, I loved him, and out of Egypt I called my son." - Hosea 11:1 (Written around 750 B.C.)


Hosea wrote this about the nation of Israel. God called Israel out of Egypt in the book of Exodus. But Matthew saw a deeper meaning. He saw that this verse also pointed to Jesus. Jesus is the true Son of God. He also came out of Egypt. It was a code.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"So he got up, took the child and his mother during the night and left for Egypt, where he stayed until the death of Herod. And so was fulfilled what the Lord had said through the prophet: 'Out of Egypt I called my son.'" - Matthew 2:14-15


King Herod was jealous. He wanted to kill the baby Jesus. An angel appeared to Joseph in a dream. The angel said, "Get up. Take the child and his mother and escape to Egypt. Stay there until I tell you." Joseph obeyed. He woke up in the middle of the night. He took Mary and Jesus and fled to Egypt. They stayed there until Herod died. The code was cracked.


The Verdict
This is a strange prophecy. It was originally about the nation of Israel. But Matthew applies it to Jesus. Jesus is the true Israel. He goes to Egypt. He comes back. It is another layer in the blueprint.


The Resonance
Jesus knows what it feels like to be displaced. He knows what it feels like to be afraid. He knows what it feels like to be a refugee. He understands your fears. He is not far away from your pain.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for understanding what it feels like to be afraid. Thank you for being with me when I am scared. Thank you for protecting me. Thank you for being my refuge. Amen.
pages.title: Day 10: The Son Called out of Egypt

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever heard a mother cry? It is a sound you never forget. It is a sound of deep pain. The Bible contains a prophecy about a mother crying. It is a prophecy about grief. It is a prophecy about the pain that comes with the birth of the Messiah. It is a code.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"This is what the LORD says: 'A voice is heard in Ramah, mourning and great weeping, Rachel weeping for her children and refusing to be comforted, because they are no more.'" - Jeremiah 31:15 (Written around 600 B.C.)


Jeremiah was writing about the exile of Israel. The people of Israel were being taken away to Babylon. Rachel was the mother of Joseph and Benjamin. She was a symbol of all the mothers of Israel. The prophecy says she is weeping. She is crying for her children. They are gone.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"When Herod realized that he had been outwitted by the Magi, he was furious, and he gave orders to kill all the boys in Bethlehem and its vicinity who were two years old and under..." - Matthew 2:16


When the wise men did not return to King Herod, he was furious. He ordered that all the boys in Bethlehem who were two years old and under be killed. He wanted to kill Jesus. But he killed all the other boys. The mothers of Bethlehem wept. They cried for their children. The prophecy was fulfilled. The code was cracked.


The Verdict
This is a dark prophecy. It is a prophecy about human evil. King Herod was a tyrant. He killed innocent children. But even in this darkness, the prophecy was fulfilled. The Bible does not shy away from human suffering.


The Resonance
The Bible does not ignore pain. It enters into it. God is with you in your grief. He sees your tears. He collects them in a bottle. You are not alone in your sorrow.


The Prayer
God, you see my tears. You know my pain. Thank you for not ignoring my suffering. Thank you for being with me in the darkness. Comfort me today. Comfort those who are grieving. Amen.
pages.title: Day 11: The Weeping of Rachel

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever been to a concert? Before the main act comes on, there is usually a warm up act. Someone comes out and gets the crowd excited. In the Bible, there was a warm up act for Jesus. His name was John the Baptist. He was a voice in the wilderness. It is a code.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"A voice of one calling: 'In the wilderness prepare the way for the LORD; make straight in the desert a highway for our God.'" - Isaiah 40:3 (Written around 700 B.C.)


Isaiah wrote about a voice in the wilderness. This voice would cry out. It would tell people to prepare the way for the Lord. It would tell them to make a straight highway in the desert. This was a metaphor. It meant that someone was coming. Someone great was coming. The people needed to get ready. It was a code.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"In those days John the Baptist came, preaching in the wilderness of Judea and saying, 'Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near.'" - Matthew 3:1-3


John the Baptist was that voice. He lived in the wilderness. He wore clothes made of camel hair. He ate locusts and wild honey. He preached a message of repentance. He told people to get ready. He told them Jesus was coming. He was the warm up act. The code was cracked.


The Verdict
The Jews were waiting for this voice. They knew the prophecy. They asked John if he was the Messiah. He said no. He said he was just a voice. He was just a warm up act. Jesus was the main act.


The Resonance
Every spiritual awakening begins with preparation. A voice cries out. A heart gets ready. God wants to prepare you for something new. He is calling. He is preparing. Are you listening?


The Prayer
God, thank you for the voices that point to Jesus. Thank you for the people who prepared the way for me to know you. Prepare my heart for what you have for me. Help me to be ready. Amen.
pages.title: Day 12: The Voice in the Wilderness

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever been to a doctor? You go in with a problem. The doctor listens. The doctor examines. The doctor gives you a prescription. In the Bible, the Messiah is described as a doctor. But He does not just heal the body. He heals the soul. It is a code.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"The Spirit of the Sovereign LORD is on me, because the LORD has anointed me to proclaim good news to the poor. He has sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim freedom for the captives and release from darkness for the prisoners..." - Isaiah 61:1 (Written around 700 B.C.)


Isaiah is speaking about the Messiah. He says the Spirit of the Lord is on Him. He says the Lord has anointed Him. Anointed means chosen and empowered. He is anointed to do four things. First, He will proclaim good news to the poor. Second, He will bind up the brokenhearted. Third, He will proclaim freedom for the captives. Fourth, He will release prisoners from darkness. It is a code.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"He went to Nazareth, where he had been brought up, and on the Sabbath day he went into the synagogue, as was his custom. He stood up to read, and the scroll of the prophet Isaiah was handed to him. Unrolling it, he found the place where it is written: 'The Spirit of the Lord is on me...' Then he began to say to them, 'Today this scripture is fulfilled in your hearing.'" - Luke 4:16-21


Jesus went to His hometown. He went to the synagogue. He stood up to read. They handed Him the scroll of Isaiah. He found this exact passage. He read it out loud. Then He rolled up the scroll. He sat down. And He said, "Today this scripture is fulfilled in your hearing." Jesus claimed to be the Messiah. He claimed to be the doctor. The code was cracked.


The Verdict
Jesus quoted this passage and applied it to Himself. He was not shy about it. He told the people in His hometown that He was the one Isaiah wrote about. This is another clue.


The Resonance
This is your inheritance. Jesus came to heal your broken heart. He came to set you free. He came to give you good news. Are you broken? Are you captive? He is the healer.


The Prayer
Jesus, you are the healer. Thank you for binding up my broken heart. Thank you for setting me free from the things that hold me captive. Thank you for the good news. Heal me today. Amen.
pages.title: Day 13: The Spirit of the Lord

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever been in a dark room? Maybe you were in a basement. Maybe the power went out. You could not see anything. You groped for a light switch. You wanted light. The Bible says the people of Galilee were walking in darkness. But they saw a great light. It is a code.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"Nevertheless, there will be no more gloom for those who were in distress. In the past he humbled the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, but in the future he will honor Galilee of the nations, by the Way of the Sea, beyond the Jordan. The people walking in darkness have seen a great light; on those living in the land of deep darkness a light has dawned." - Isaiah 9:1-2 (Written around 700 B.C.)


Isaiah is talking about the land of Galilee. This was a region in northern Israel. It was a region that had been humbled. It had been invaded. It was a land of darkness. But Isaiah said the people walking in darkness would see a great light. This was a prophecy. It meant that the Messiah would bring light to Galilee. It was a code.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"Leaving Nazareth, he went and lived in Capernaum, which was by the lake in the area of Zebulun and Naphtali, to fulfill what was said through the prophet Isaiah: 'Land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali, the Way of the Sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles, the people living in darkness have seen a great light; on those living in the land of the shadow of death a light has dawned.'" - Matthew 4:13-16


Jesus left Nazareth. He went to Capernaum. This was in Galilee. This was in the area of Zebulun and Naphtali. He began His ministry there. He preached. He healed. He cast out demons. He was the light in the darkness. Matthew tells us this happened to fulfill the prophecy. The code was cracked.


The Verdict
This is a geographical prophecy. It said the Messiah would bring light to Galilee. Jesus brought light to Galilee. It is another detail that lines up perfectly.


The Resonance
God meets you where you are. No place is too dark for His light to reach. No heart is too hard. He brings light.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the light in the darkness. Thank you for shining your light in the dark places. Shine your light into my heart today. Shine your light into my home. Amen.
pages.title: Day 14: The Light in Galilee

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever been rejected? Maybe you were rejected by a school. Maybe you were rejected by a friend. Maybe you were rejected by a job. Rejection hurts. It is one of the deepest pains we can experience. The Bible tells us that the Messiah would be rejected. He would be a rejected stone. It is a code.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone; the LORD has done this, and it is marvelous in our eyes." - Psalm 118:22 (Written around 500 B.C.)


The Psalmist is writing about a stone. The builders looked at this stone and they said, "No, that stone is no good. We do not want that stone." So they threw it away. But then something happened. That rejected stone became the cornerstone. The cornerstone is the most important stone in a building. It sets the angles. It holds the structure together. It is a code.


The Fulfillment (NT)
*"Jesus said to them, 'Have you never read in the Scriptures: "The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone; the Lord has done this, and it is marvelous in our eyes"?'
…..
pages.title: Day 15: The Rejected Stone

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Fulfillment (NT)
"Jesus said to them, 'Have you never read in the Scriptures: "The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone; the Lord has done this, and it is marvelous in our eyes"?'" - Matthew 21:42


Jesus quoted this Psalm. He applied it to Himself. He was the stone. The religious leaders were the builders. They looked at Jesus and they said, "No, we do not want Him. He is not the Messiah we want." So they rejected Him. They killed Him. But God raised Him from the dead. He became the cornerstone of the church. The code was cracked.


The Verdict
This is a prophecy about rejection and vindication. The Messiah would be rejected. But He would be exalted. Jesus was rejected. He was crucified. But He rose again. He is now the cornerstone.


The Resonance
When others reject you, remember that God sees your worth. You are not a rejected stone. You are a cornerstone. You are part of God's building. You are important. You are valuable.


The Prayer
God, thank you that you see my worth. Thank you that you do not reject me. Thank you that Jesus was rejected so that I could be accepted. Help me to find my worth in you. Help me to stop looking for approval from others. Amen.
pages.title: Day 15: The Rejected Stone (Continued)

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever been hated? Maybe someone hated you for no reason. You did not do anything to them. You did not hurt them. They just did not like you. It is a confusing feeling. The Bible says the Messiah would be hated without a cause. It is a code.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"Those who hate me without reason outnumber the hairs of my head; many are my enemies without cause, those who seek to destroy me. I am forced to restore what I did not steal." - Psalm 69:4 (Written around 1000 B.C.)


David wrote this Psalm. He was being chased by his enemies. He was being hunted like an animal. He said, "Those who hate me without reason outnumber the hairs of my head." He was saying he had a lot of enemies. And they hated him for no reason. This is a prophecy. It points to the Messiah. It is a code.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"But this is to fulfill what is written in their Law: 'They hated me without reason.'" - John 15:25


Jesus quoted this Psalm. He told His disciples that the world would hate them. He said, "If the world hates you, keep in mind that it hated me first." He said the world hated Him without a reason. The religious leaders hated Him. The crowds turned on Him. He was hated without a cause. The code was cracked.


The Verdict
This is a prophecy about the rejection of the Messiah. He would be hated. Not because He did something wrong. But because the world was blind. Jesus was hated without a cause.


The Resonance
Sometimes the most profound things are the most hated by the world. If you are hated for doing the right thing, you are in good company. Jesus knows what it feels like. He understands.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for enduring hatred for me. Thank you for loving me even when others hated you. Help me to love those who hate me. Help me to forgive those who hurt me. Amen.
pages.title: Day 16: Hated Without a Cause

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever been betrayed by a friend? Maybe a friend shared a secret you told them. Maybe a friend stabbed you in the back. Maybe a friend abandoned you when you needed them most. Betrayal is one of the deepest wounds. The Bible says the Messiah would be betrayed by a close friend. It is a code.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"Even my close friend, someone I trusted, one who shared my bread, has turned against me." - Psalm 41:9 (Written around 1000 B.C.)


David wrote this Psalm. He was talking about a close friend who had betrayed him. He said, "Even my close friend, someone I trusted, one who shared my bread, has turned against me." Sharing bread was a sign of friendship. It meant sharing a meal. It meant intimacy. But this friend turned against him. It is a code.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"I am not referring to all of you; I know those I have chosen. But this is to fulfill this passage of Scripture: 'He who shared my bread has turned against me.'" - John 13:18


Jesus quoted this Psalm at the Last Supper. He was talking about Judas. Judas was one of His twelve disciples. Judas shared bread with Jesus. Judas was His friend. But Judas betrayed Him. He sold Him for thirty pieces of silver. He kissed Him in the garden. He handed Him over to the soldiers. The code was cracked.


The Verdict
This is a prophecy about intimate betrayal. The Messiah would be betrayed by someone close to Him. Someone who shared His bread. Jesus was betrayed by Judas. The prophecy was fulfilled.


The Resonance
The greatest pain is not from enemies. It is from those we trust. If you have been betrayed by a friend, Jesus understands. He knows that pain. He will heal it.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for understanding the pain of betrayal. Thank you for being a friend who never betrays. Heal my heart from the wounds of broken friendships. Help me to trust again. Amen.
pages.title: Day 17: The Betrayal of a Friend

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever bought something really cheap? Maybe you bought a shirt at a garage sale for a dollar. Maybe you found a bargain at the store. It feels good to get a deal. But in the Bible, there is a prophecy about a cheap price. It is a prophecy about the price of a life. It is a code.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"I told them, 'If you think it best, give me my pay; but if not, keep it.' So they paid me thirty pieces of silver. And the LORD said to me, 'Throw it to the potter'—the handsome price at which they valued me! So I took the thirty pieces of silver and threw them to the potter at the house of the LORD." - Zechariah 11:12-13 (Written around 500 B.C.)


Zechariah is a prophet. He is acting out a prophecy. He is playing the role of the shepherd. He asks the people for his pay. They pay him thirty pieces of silver. This is a low price. It was the price of a slave. Then God tells him to throw the silver to the potter. The potter was a craftsman. The silver would be used to buy a field. This is a strange prophecy. It is a code.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"Then one of the Twelve—the one called Judas Iscariot—went to the chief priests and asked, 'What are you willing to give me if I deliver him over to you?' So they counted out for him thirty pieces of silver." - Matthew 26:14-15


Judas went to the chief priests. He asked them how much they would pay him to betray Jesus. They counted out thirty pieces of silver. This was the exact price Zechariah predicted. Judas betrayed Jesus for thirty pieces of silver. The code was cracked.


The Verdict
This is an incredibly specific prophecy. It predicts the exact amount of money. It predicts the exact price of betrayal. Jesus was sold for thirty pieces of silver. This is not a coincidence. This is evidence.


The Resonance
Jesus allowed Himself to be valued at the price of a slave. Not because He was worth that much. But because He valued YOU that much. You are worth everything to Him.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for valuing me enough to humble yourself. Thank you for allowing yourself to be sold for thirty pieces of silver. Thank you for loving me that much. Help me to see my worth in you. Amen.
pages.title: Day 18: Sold for Thirty Pieces of Silver

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever been in a situation where you wanted to defend yourself? Someone accused you of something you did not do. Someone lied about you. You wanted to speak up. You wanted to clear your name. But the Bible says the Messiah would be silent. He would not defend Himself. It is a code.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"He was oppressed and afflicted, yet he did not open his mouth; he was led like a lamb to the slaughter, and as a sheep before its shearers is silent, so he did not open his mouth." - Isaiah 53:7 (Written around 700 B.C.)


Isaiah is describing the suffering servant. He is describing the Messiah. He says the Messiah would be oppressed. He would be afflicted. But he would not open his mouth. He would be led like a lamb to the slaughter. He would be silent. This is a prophecy about the trial of Jesus. It is a code.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"When he was accused by the chief priests and the elders, he gave no answer. Then Pilate asked him, 'Don't you hear the testimony they are bringing against you?' But Jesus made no reply, not even to a single charge—to the great amazement of the governor." - Matthew 27:12-14


Jesus was brought before Pilate. The chief priests and elders accused him. They made false charges. They lied about him. Pilate asked Jesus, "Don't you hear what they are saying?" Jesus said nothing. He did not defend himself. He was silent. Pilate was amazed. The code was cracked.


The Verdict
This is a prophecy about the behavior of the Messiah during his trial. He would be silent. Jesus was silent. He did not fight back. He did not argue. He was like a lamb before its shearers.


The Resonance
Sometimes the most powerful thing you can do is be silent. Trusting God in the face of false accusations is a sign of strength. You do not have to fight every battle. God will fight for you.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being silent so that I could speak to God. Thank you for enduring false accusations. Help me to trust you when I am accused. Help me to be silent when I need to be. Amen.
pages.title: Day 19: The Silence Before the Slaughter

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever been scared? Have you ever run away from something? When I was a kid, I ran away from a dog. It was a big dog. It barked at me. I ran. The Bible says the disciples ran away when Jesus was arrested. They were scared. They were like scattered sheep. It is a code.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"Awake, sword, against my shepherd, against the man who is close to me! declares the LORD Almighty. Strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered, and I will turn my hand against the little ones." - Zechariah 13:7 (Written around 500 B.C.)


Zechariah says the sword will strike the shepherd. The shepherd will be smitten. He will be struck down. And then the sheep will be scattered. The sheep will run away. This is a prophecy about the death of Jesus and the flight of the disciples. It is a code.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"Then Jesus told them, 'This very night you will all fall away on account of me, for it is written: "I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered."'" - Matthew 26:31


Jesus quoted this prophecy to His disciples. He told them they would all fall away. He said the shepherd would be struck. The sheep would be scattered. That is exactly what happened. Jesus was arrested. The disciples ran away. Peter denied Him. They all fled. The code was cracked.


The Verdict
This is a prophecy about the disciples. They were the sheep. They would scatter. Jesus was the shepherd. He would be struck. It happened exactly as it was written.


The Resonance
Even when you fail or run away, Jesus does not abandon you. He is the Good Shepherd who goes after the scattered sheep. He comes after you. He finds you. He brings you back.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for never giving up on me. Thank you for coming after me when I run away. Thank you for being the Good Shepherd. Help me to stop running. Help me to stay close to you. Amen.
pages.title: Day 20: The Smitten Shepherd

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever been in the wrong place at the wrong time? Maybe you were blamed for something you did not do. The Bible says the Messiah would be counted with criminals. He would be treated like a bad guy. It is a code.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"Therefore I will give him a portion among the great, and he will divide the spoils with the strong, because he poured out his life unto death, and was numbered with the transgressors. For he bore the sin of many, and made intercession for the transgressors." - Isaiah 53:12 (Written around 700 B.C.)


Isaiah says the Messiah would be numbered with the transgressors. Transgressors are criminals. They are lawbreakers. The Messiah would be treated like a criminal. He would be crucified with criminals. But He would also pray for them. It is a code.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"Two other men, both criminals, were also led out with him to be executed. When they came to the place called the Skull, they crucified him there, along with the criminals—one on his right, the other on his left. Jesus said, 'Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing.'" - Luke 23:32-34


Jesus was crucified between two criminals. He was treated like a bad guy. He was numbered with the transgressors. And He prayed for them. He said, "Father, forgive them." He was forgiving the people who were killing Him. The code was cracked.


The Verdict
This is a prophecy about the method of execution. The Messiah would be crucified with criminals. Jesus was crucified with criminals. The prophecy was fulfilled.


The Resonance
The innocent was treated like the guilty so the guilty could be set free. Jesus took your place. He was numbered with the criminals so you could be numbered with the saints.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being numbered with the criminals so I could be numbered with the saints. Thank you for forgiving me. Thank you for taking my place. Help me to forgive others. Amen.
pages.title: Day 21: Crucified with Sinners

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever had a wound? Maybe you cut your finger. Maybe you had a broken bone. A wound is a mark. It is evidence of pain. The Bible says the Messiah would have wounds in His hands and His feet. It says they would be pierced. It is a code.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"Dogs surround me, a pack of villains encircles me; they pierce my hands and my feet." - Psalm 22:16 (Written around 1000 B.C.)


David wrote this Psalm. He is describing a scene of suffering. He says, "Dogs surround me. A pack of villains encircles me. They pierce my hands and my feet." He is describing a person being attacked by enemies. This is a prophecy. It points to the crucifixion. It is a code.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"So the other disciples told him, 'We have seen the Lord!' But he said to them, 'Unless I see the nail marks in his hands and put my finger where the nails were, and put my hand into his side, I will not believe.'" - John 20:25


Thomas was not with the other disciples when Jesus appeared to them. He said, "Unless I see the nail marks in his hands and put my finger where the nails were, I will not believe." A week later, Jesus appeared again. He said to Thomas, "Put your finger here; see my hands. Reach out your hand and put it into my side." Thomas saw the nail marks. He saw the pierced hands and feet. The code was cracked.


The Verdict
Crucifixion did not exist when David wrote this Psalm. It was invented by the Romans a thousand years later. The fact that David predicted pierced hands and feet is stunning. It is a major clue.


The Resonance
The scars of Jesus are proof of His love for you. He bears those marks for eternity. He is not ashamed of them. He is not ashamed of you.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for the scars you bear for me. Thank you for the nail marks in your hands. Thank you for loving me that much. Help me to never forget your sacrifice. Amen.
pages.title: Day 22: Hands and Feet Pierced

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever been mocked? Maybe someone made fun of your clothes. Maybe someone laughed at your accent. Maybe someone ridiculed your faith. Mocking hurts. It is a public humiliation. The Bible says the Messiah would be mocked. It is a code.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"All who see me mock me; they hurl insults, shaking their heads. 'He trusts in the LORD,' they say, 'let the LORD rescue him. Let him deliver him, since he delights in him.'" - Psalm 22:7-8 (Written around 1000 B.C.)


David is describing the mockers. They mock him. They hurl insults. They shake their heads. They say, "He trusts in the LORD. Let the LORD rescue him." This is a prophecy. It points to the crucifixion of Jesus. It is a code.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"Those who passed by hurled insults at him, shaking their heads and saying, 'You who are going to destroy the temple and build it in three days, save yourself! Come down from the cross, if you are the Son of God!' In the same way the chief priests, the teachers of the law and the elders mocked him. 'He saved others,' they said, 'but he can't save himself! He's the king of Israel! Let him come down now from the cross, and we will believe in him. He trusts in God. Let God rescue him now if he wants him, for he said, "I am the Son of God."'" - Matthew 27:39-43


This is exactly what happened at the crucifixion. The people passed by. They hurled insults at Jesus. They shook their heads. They said, "He trusts in God. Let God rescue him." The chief priests mocked him. The teachers of the law mocked him. The elders mocked him. They used the exact words of the Psalm. The code was cracked.


The Verdict
This is a prophecy about the mockery of the Messiah. The exact words of the mockers were predicted a thousand years before they said them. This is an incredible detail. This is evidence.


The Resonance
When people mock your faith, remember that you are in good company. Jesus faced the same thing and overcame it. You will overcome too.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for enduring mockery for me. Thank you for not coming down from the cross. Help me to stand strong when my faith is mocked. Help me to forgive those who mock me. Amen.
pages.title: Day 23: Mocked and Shaken Heads

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever been thirsty? Really thirsty? Maybe you ran a race. Maybe you were outside on a hot day. Thirst is a powerful feeling. The Bible says the Messiah would be thirsty on the cross. And He would be given something strange to drink. It is a code.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"They put gall in my food and gave me vinegar for my thirst." - Psalm 69:21 (Written around 1000 B.C.)


David wrote this Psalm. He is describing his suffering. He says, "They put gall in my food and gave me vinegar for my thirst." Gall is a bitter substance. It comes from a plant. It is poison. Vinegar is sour wine. This is a prophecy. It points to the crucifixion. It is a code.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"There they offered Jesus wine to drink, mixed with gall; but after tasting it, he refused to drink it. Later, knowing that everything had now been finished, and so that Scripture would be fulfilled, Jesus said, 'I am thirsty.' A jar of wine vinegar was there, so they soaked a sponge in it, put the sponge on a stalk of the hyssop plant, and lifted it to Jesus' lips." - Matthew 27:34; John 19:28-29


The soldiers offered Jesus wine mixed with gall. This was a painkiller. It was meant to dull the pain. Jesus tasted it and refused to drink it. He wanted to feel the full pain. Later, He said, "I am thirsty." They gave Him vinegar. The prophecy was fulfilled. The code was cracked.


The Verdict
This is a prophecy about the smallest details of the crucifixion. It predicts the gall and the vinegar. Jesus experienced both. This is another clue.


The Resonance
Even in suffering, Jesus fulfilled the smallest details of prophecy. He is a God of precision and love. He cares about the details.


The Prayer
God, I trust you even in the small painful details of my life. Thank you for fulfilling every detail of the prophecy. Thank you for your precision. Help me to trust you with the details. Amen.
pages.title: Day 24: Given Gall and Vinegar

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever played a game of chance? Maybe you flipped a coin. Maybe you rolled a dice. Maybe you played the lottery. It is a game of luck. The Bible says the soldiers would play a game of chance for the clothes of Jesus. It is a code.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"They divide my clothes among them and cast lots for my garment." - Psalm 22:18 (Written around 1000 B.C.)


David is describing the scene at the crucifixion. He says, "They divide my clothes among them and cast lots for my garment." The soldiers divided the clothes of the condemned man. They cast lots for the expensive pieces. This is a prophecy. It is a code.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"When the soldiers crucified Jesus, they took his clothes, dividing them into four shares, one for each of them, with the undergarment remaining. This garment was seamless, woven in one piece from top to bottom. 'Let's not tear it,' they said to one another. 'Let's decide by lot who will get it.' This happened that the scripture might be fulfilled..." - John 19:23-24


The soldiers took the clothes of Jesus. They divided them into four shares. One for each soldier. But the undergarment was seamless. It was woven in one piece. They said, "Let's not tear it. Let's cast lots for it." So they gambled for the garment. The prophecy was fulfilled. The code was cracked.


The Verdict
This is a prophecy about the random actions of the soldiers. They did not know they were fulfilling prophecy. They were just doing their job. But God used their random actions to fulfill His word.


The Resonance
Nothing that happens to you is outside of God's plan. Even the smallest details of your life are in His hands. He is in control.


The Prayer
Thank you, God, for being in control of every detail. Even the random things in my life are under your care. Help me to trust you. Help me to rest in your sovereignty. Amen.
pages.title: Day 25: Garments Divided by Lot

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever felt alone? Really alone? Maybe you were in a new city. Maybe you were in a hospital. Maybe you were in a dark room. Loneliness is a painful feeling. The Bible says the Messiah would feel forsaken by God. It is a code.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"My God, my God, why have you forsaken me? Why are you so far from saving me, so far from my cries of anguish?" - Psalm 22:1 (Written around 1000 B.C.)


David wrote this Psalm. He felt abandoned by God. He felt forsaken. He cried out, "My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?" This is a prophecy. It points to the cry of Jesus on the cross. It is a code.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"About three in the afternoon Jesus cried out in a loud voice, 'Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani?' (which means 'My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?')." - Matthew 27:46


Jesus quoted this Psalm on the cross. He cried out, "My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?" He was quoting the first line of a Psalm that describes His own crucifixion. He was feeling the weight of the sin of the world. He was separated from the Father. The code was cracked.


The Verdict
This is a prophecy about the spiritual agony of the Messiah. He would feel forsaken. Jesus felt forsaken. He took our sin upon Himself.


The Resonance
Because Jesus experienced separation from God on the cross, you will never have to. You have permanent access to the Father. You will never be forsaken.


The Prayer
Thank you, Jesus, that I will never be forsaken. Thank you for experiencing separation so that I could experience acceptance. Thank you for the access I have to the Father. Help me to never take that for granted. Amen.
pages.title: Day 26: The Cry of Forsakenness

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever been to a funeral? It is a sad occasion. People gather to mourn. They gather to remember. The Bible says the Messiah would have a specific burial. He would be buried in a rich man's tomb. It is a code.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"He was assigned a grave with the wicked, and with the rich in his death, though he had done no violence, nor was any deceit in his mouth." - Isaiah 53:9 (Written around 700 B.C.)


Isaiah says the Messiah would be assigned a grave with the wicked. This meant He would die among criminals. But Isaiah also says He would be with the rich in His death. This is a paradox. How can you be buried with the wicked and with the rich? The answer is in the details of the crucifixion. It is a code.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"As evening approached, there came a rich man from Arimathea, named Joseph, who had himself become a disciple of Jesus. Going to Pilate, he asked for Jesus' body, and Pilate ordered that it be given to him. Joseph took the body, wrapped it in a clean linen cloth, and placed it in his own new tomb that he had cut out of the rock." - Matthew 27:57-60


Joseph of Arimathea was a rich man. He was a disciple of Jesus. He went to Pilate. He asked for the body of Jesus. Pilate gave it to him. Joseph took the body. He wrapped it in a clean linen cloth. He placed it in his own new tomb. This was a rich man's tomb. The prophecy was fulfilled. The code was cracked.


The Verdict
This is a prophecy about the burial of the Messiah. He would be buried by a rich man. Jesus was buried by Joseph of Arimathea. The prophecy was fulfilled in detail.


The Resonance
Even in death, God honored His Son. He will honor you too. He will take care of your final resting place. He will take care of your legacy.


The Prayer
God, I trust you to honor me in my life and in my death. Thank you for the hope of the resurrection. Thank you for the empty tomb. Help me to live with eternity in mind. Amen.
pages.title: Day 27: Buried in a Rich Man's Tomb

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever been to a cemetery? It is a place of silence. It is a place of endings. But the Bible says the Messiah would not stay in the grave. He would rise again. It is a code.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"Therefore my heart is glad and my tongue rejoices; my body also will rest secure, because you will not abandon me to the realm of the dead, nor will you let your faithful one see decay." - Psalm 16:9-10 (Written around 1000 B.C.)


David wrote this Psalm. He said his body would rest secure. He said God would not abandon him to the realm of the dead. He said God would not let his faithful one see decay. This is a prophecy. It points to the resurrection. It is a code.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"Seeing what was to come, he spoke of the resurrection of the Messiah, that he was not abandoned to the realm of the dead, nor did his body see decay. God has raised this Jesus to life, and we are all witnesses of it." - Acts 2:31-32


Peter preached this on the day of Pentecost. He said David was a prophet. He said David knew the Messiah would rise from the dead. He said the Messiah would not be abandoned to the realm of the dead. His body would not see decay. Peter said this was fulfilled in Jesus. God raised Jesus to life. The code was cracked.


The Verdict
This is the cornerstone of the Christian faith. The tomb is empty. Jesus rose from the dead. The prophecy was fulfilled. This is the ultimate clue.


The Resonance
Death is not the end of the story. The grave is not the final word. Jesus is alive. And because He is alive, you will live forever.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for rising from the dead. Thank you for defeating death. Thank you that the grave is empty. Because you live, I will live forever. Help me to live in the power of your resurrection. Amen.
pages.title: Day 28: Not Left in the Grave

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever won a championship? Maybe your team won a game. Maybe you won a prize. It feels good to win. You lift the trophy. You celebrate. The Bible says the Messiah would win the ultimate victory. He would ascend on high. It is a code.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"When you ascended on high, you took many captives; you received gifts from people, even from the rebellious—that you, LORD God, might dwell there." - Psalm 68:18 (Written around 1000 B.C.)


David wrote this Psalm. He is describing a victorious king. The king ascends on high. He takes captives. He receives gifts. This is a prophecy. It points to the ascension of Jesus. It is a code.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"This is why it says: 'When he ascended on high, he took many captives and gave gifts to his people.'" - Ephesians 4:8


Paul quotes this Psalm. He applies it to Jesus. Jesus ascended on high. He took many captives. He gave gifts to His people. He ascended into heaven. He is seated at the right hand of the Father. He has won the victory. The code was cracked.


The Verdict
This is a prophecy about the ascension of the Messiah. He would ascend on high. He would take captives. He would give gifts. Jesus ascended on high. He gives gifts to His people.


The Resonance
Jesus has taken back the keys of death and hell. You have access to His victory and His gifts. You are on the winning team.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for sharing your victory with me. Thank you for the gifts you give me. Thank you for ascending on high. Help me to walk in your victory. Help me to use your gifts for your glory. Amen.

pages.body:
The Hook
Have you ever seen a king? Maybe you saw a picture of a king. Maybe you saw a movie about a king. A king sits on a throne. A king rules a kingdom. The Bible says the Messiah would have an eternal throne. It is a code.


The Ancient Text (OT)
"In my vision at night I looked, and there before me was one like a son of man, coming with the clouds of heaven. He approached the Ancient of Days and was led into his presence. He was given authority, glory and sovereign power; all nations and peoples of every language worshiped him. His dominion is an everlasting dominion that will not pass away, and his kingdom is one that will never be destroyed." - Daniel 7:13-14 (Written around 600 B.C.)


Daniel saw a vision. He saw one like a son of man. He came with the clouds of heaven. He approached the Ancient of Days. He was given authority. He was given glory. He was given sovereign power. All nations worshiped him. His dominion is everlasting. His kingdom will never be destroyed. It is a code.


The Fulfillment (NT)
"The seventh angel sounded his trumpet, and there were loud voices in heaven, which said: 'The kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord and of his Messiah, and he will reign for ever and ever.'" - Revelation 11:15


This is the final fulfillment. The kingdom of the world becomes the kingdom of our Lord. Jesus reigns forever. His kingdom will never end. The code was cracked.


The Verdict
This is the final clue. The blueprint does not end with a cross. It ends with a crown. Jesus is the King of Kings. His throne is eternal.


The Resonance
The story is not just a historical mystery. It is a future reality. The story is not over. Jesus is coming back. He will reign forever. And you will reign with Him.


The Prayer
Jesus, I give my life to you. Take my life and use it for your kingdom. Thank you for the hope of eternity. Thank you for the promise of a forever kingdom. Come, Lord Jesus. Amen.



END MATTER


The 300+ Prophecy Challenge
We only looked at 30 prophecies in this book. The Bible contains over 300 prophecies about Jesus. If you want to keep investigating, I challenge you to read the Gospel of John. It is 21 chapters. It tells the story of Jesus from the perspective of an eyewitness. As you read, look for the clues. Look for the prophecies. Look for the evidence. You will be amazed at what you find.


The Probability Factor
Mathematicians have calculated the probability of one person fulfilling just eight of these prophecies. The odds are 1 in 10 to the 17th power. That is a one with seventeen zeros after it. That is the same as covering the entire state of Texas with silver coins, marking one coin, and having a blindfolded person pick the right coin on the first try. Jesus fulfilled not eight. Not thirty. Over three hundred. The math points to a miracle.


A Note on Faith
Evidence is important. It satisfies the mind. But evidence does not save you. The evidence points to a person. The evidence points to Jesus. You can believe the facts and still be far from God. The invitation is for your heart. Jesus said, "Here I am! I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, I will come in." The evidence is on the table. The door is open. It is your choice.


About the Author
Christine A. writes for the spiritually curious. He is passionate about showing people the evidence that the Bible is true. He lives with his family and enjoys good coffee and long conversations with skeptics. He believes that honest questions deserve honest answers.


Coming Next: Written in the Stars
If you enjoyed this journey, the next book in the series goes deeper. Written in the Stars takes a 30 day look at the impossible prophecies that point to Jesus. It is for the seeker who wants to go further.


Final Call to Action
Scan the QR code below to get the next book in the series. Visit our website to download a free reading plan. Join our community of seekers. The investigation is not over. The adventure is just beginning.
